quickSummary: Amino acids are substituted methanes with an α-amino, α-carboxyl, hydrogen, and variable R group. At physiological pH, they exist as dipolar Zwitterions with net charge zero at their isoelectric point (pI). All 19 standard amino acids are chiral except Glycine (R = -H). Peptide bonds (-CO-NH-) have 40% partial double bond character, enforcing rigidity and coplanarity. Backbone rotation is restricted to torsional angles Phi (φ) and Psi (ψ), mapped on the Ramachandran Plot.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Amino acids are organic compounds containing an amino group and an acidic carboxyl group substituted on the same $\alpha$-carbon atom ($\alpha$-amino acids).

### Zwitterionic State & Isoelectric Point (pI)
At physiological $\text{pH } (\approx 7.4)$, the carboxyl group loses a proton ($-\text{COO}^-$) and the amino group gains a proton ($-\text{NH}_3^+$), forming a dipolar **Zwitterion**:
$$\Large \mathbf{\text{pI} = \frac{\text{pK}_{a1} (\text{COOH}) + \text{pK}_{a2} (\text{NH}_3^+)}{2}}$$

• **Chirality Exception**: All standard amino acids are chiral (optically active) **EXCEPT Glycine ($R = -\text{H}$)**, which is symmetric and **achiral**.

AMINO ACID TAXONOMY
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                           ▼                           ▼
   NON-POLAR / HYDROPHOBIC      POLAR UNCHARGED            CHARGED (Acidic / Basic)
  ├── Glycine (Achiral)        ├── Cysteine (-SH)          ├── Acidic: Aspartate (-COO⁻)
  ├── Alanine, Valine, Leucine ├── Serine, Threonine       ├── Acidic: Glutamate (-COO⁻)
  ├── Proline (Imino acid)     ├── Asparagine, Glutamine   ├── Basic: Lysine (-NH₃⁺)
  ├── Methionine (Sulfur)      └── Tyrosine                ├── Basic: Arginine (Guanidino)
  └── Tryptophan (Indole)                                  └── Basic: Histidine (Imidazole)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Non-Polar**: Glycine, Alanine, Valine, Leucine, Isoleucine, Proline (imino acid), Phenylalanine, Methionine, Tryptophan.
• **Polar Uncharged**: Serine, Threonine, Cysteine (forms disulfide bonds), Asparagine, Glutamine, Tyrosine.
• **Acidic (Negatively Charged)**: Aspartate, Glutamate.
• **Basic (Positively Charged)**: Lysine, Arginine (guanidino group), Histidine (imidazole ring).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Peptide Bond Geometry & Ramachandran Plot
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Peptide Bond Geometry & Ramachandran Plot
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PEPTIDE BOND FORMATION
                            
    R₁                       R₂                        R₁       H   R₂
    │                        │                         │        │   │
  H₂N─C─COOH  +  H─NH─C─COOH  ──[−H₂O]──►  H₂N─C──C ── N ── C─COOH
      │               │                         │  ║   ║    │
      H               H                         H  O   O    H
                                                   [Peptide Bond]
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Resonance & Planarity**: Delocalization of the carbonyl $\pi$-electrons gives the $\text{C}-\text{N}$ peptide bond **40% partial double bond character**. Hence, the six atoms of the peptide unit ($\text{C}_\alpha-\text{C}=\text{O}-\text{N}-\text{H}-\text{C}_\alpha$) are rigid, coplanar, and cannot freely rotate.
• **Torsional Angles**: Rotation occurs exclusively around:
  - **Phi ($\phi$)**: Rotation angle around the $\text{N}-\text{C}_\alpha$ bond.
  - **Psi ($\psi$)**: Rotation angle around the $\text{C}_\alpha-\text{C}$ bond.
• **The Ramachandran Plot (1963)**: A 2D steric plot of $\phi$ versus $\psi$ defining permissible conformational space for right-handed $\alpha$-helices, $\beta$-sheets, and collagen triple helices.
